To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the multivariate geospatial algorithm is a useful tool to optimize rain gauge networks and to predict rainfall in unrecorded locations; (ii) the digital elevation model is the most important variable for predicting rainfall, followed by humidity and temperature; and (iii) the multivariate algorithm can provide more accurate spatial predictions of rainfall than linear regression, especially in mountainous areas.

the optimal rain gauge network design and the multivariate geostatical analysis are useful tools to reduce the number of rainfall gauging stations and improve the spatial prediction of the monthly rainfall.
the multivariate kriging approach is more efficient in spatially predicting rainfall than the linear regression approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimal design of a rain gauge network, the spatial interpolation of rainfall using multivariate geosatistical algorithms, and the spatial rainfall prediction based on collocated elevation, humidity and temperature data.
the optimal design of a rain gauge network and the estimation of point precipitation at unobserved locations using multivariate geostatical analysis.
the design of optimal rainfall stations and the development of a spatial rainfall prediction model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the digital elevation data were more important than other hydrological variables for the prediction of monthly precipitation in the study area.
the multivariate kriging algorithm outperform the univariate kriging and linear regression algorithms.
the multivariate spatial interpolation method was superior to the linear regression in terms of the spatial rainfall estimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multivariate kriging technique is a promising tool for the optimal design of a rainfall network and for spatial precipitation mapping.
a multivariate geostatistics approach can be used for rainfall data optimization and rainfall spatial prediction.
the spatial distribution of rainfall in Thailand can be predicted with reasonable accuracy using multivariate geospatial algorithms.

the spatial rainfall prediction should be performed using multivariate geostatical algorithms that consider the collocated digital elevation data and other hydrological data.
